spans.s:
hitá, ppl., adj.
 —1. put, set; placed; and
so
 —2. pregnantly (like Eng. in place, i. e.
‘in the right place,’ and Ger. gelegen,
‘lying aright, i. e. convenient’), fit, convenient,
 agreeable; yadi tatra te hitam,
if it suits thee there; advantageous, salutary;
[]
 —3. as n. welfare, safety. [√1dhā,
‘put,’ 954c: -dhita in Veda: cf. θετός,
‘set.’]

hita-kāma, a. wishing one's welfare,
well-wishing. [see kāma.]

hitecchā, f. desire for the welfare (of
another). [icchā.]
